title: Seller Conversational Economics Flashpack (rough)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, seller-facing quickpack to help SEs and AEs talk through tradeoffs for chat/assistant features. Focus: how to reduce per-conversation cost without sacrificing perceived latency/quality. Not formal pricing — tactical language and qualifying questions for pilot conversations.

Key takeaways (30s):
- Customers care about two metrics: perceived latency (response delay) and per-interaction unit cost.
- Small changes (prompt engineering, short-circuiting, prefix caching, reranking) can cut cost by 30–70% for many chat workloads.
- Default seller flow: start with hosted API pilot -> validate UX & quality -> recommend Dedicated when throughput/cost predictability is needed -> offer Private for compliance/regulatory gating.

One-line value props for convo buyers:
- Faster answers for users while reducing token spend with smart caching and lighter model fallbacks.
- Predictable unit economics at scale with Dedicated capacity and burst policies.
- Outage/latency protection: automatic routing and fallback models keep assistants alive during peak loads.

Qualify quickly (questions to ask in a discovery call):
1) What is a typical session look like? (avg turns, avg prompt length, typical doc length referenced)
2) What latency is acceptable for your user experience? (under 300ms vs 500–1,000ms vs acceptable async)
3) What percent of interactions require up-to-date or proprietary data? (affects caching & private deploy needs)
4) Expected concurrent users / peak QPS?
5) Any regulatory constraints (PII, region residency, audit logs)?

Quick heuristics (sellable recommendations):
- Low-latency consumer chat: prioritize short context window, aggressive prefix caching, small quantized model variants for first-pass responses, then async rerank with larger model if needed.
- High-quality doc-grounded assistant: keep larger models for rerank/confirmation, use embeddings + retrieval to limit prompt size, pin model versions for deterministic outputs.
- Cost-sensitive batch-ish workflows (summary/email draft): use larger batch windows and Dedicated pools.

Tactical playbook (2-minute seller script):
- SE: "Tell me about your typical conversation — average length and how often you hit long documents?" (qualify)
- If short, fast UX is critical: "We can start a pilot on our hosted API with a small footprint model + prefix caching. That usually drops token count by ~40% while keeping perceived latency near native app speed."
- If docs/heavy context: "Our retrieval + embedding pattern keeps the prompt small; we recommend a canary where we use a larger reranker only when the small model signals low confidence."
- If compliance: "We can run a Private deployment (VPC/on‑prem) with customer KMS and audit logs for the pilot — same API surface as hosted so engineers don’t rewrite code."

Objection responses (short):
- "Your pricing looks high": "We focus on unit economics — there are levers (batching, caching, lightweight first-pass models, and rerank) we can apply quickly in the pilot that typically lower per-conversation cost significantly. We’ll run a short eval on your sample traffic to give concrete numbers."
- "We can self-host cheaper": "Self-hosting hides operational burden and latency unpredictability. Redwood gives a predictable routing, autoscaling, and fallbacks layer so your app stays healthy during spikes; Dedicated can also be more cost-effective at steady-state."
- "Latency spikes worry us": "We can route hot traffic to local Dedicated pools and fallback to a smaller model during congested windows — seamless to your app and covered in our SLO docs."

Pilot checklist (what to ship in a 2–4 week pilot):
- Integration: generate keys and start with hosted API; SDK sample in client repo (we provide).
- Metrics to capture: mean latency (p50/p95), tokens per turn, % interactions using fallback/secondary model, cost per 1k interactions estimate.
- Evaluation prompts: 50–100 representative sessions (we’ll provide a template).
- Success criteria: 20–40% reduction in token spend or meeting latency SLOs and qualitative UX signoff.

Canary & fallback cheat sheet (operations-friendly notes):
- Primary model: tuned for quality.
- Secondary model: faster, lower-token-cost variant (quantized) used when queue/backpressure detected.
- Routing policy: latency-first for consumer; cost-first for internal automation jobs.
- Alerts: p95 latency degraded, fallback rate > 5% for > 5 minutes, token spend > forecast by 15%.

Differentiators we can call out on calls (short bullets):
- Same API and rollout controls across Hosted, Dedicated, Private -> no rework as you migrate.
- Smart prefix/KV caching that is workload-aware (not just naive LRU).
- Built-in rerank/verify workflows to keep perceived quality high while saving tokens.

Appendix: quick technical notes to hand to an engineer during the call (copy/paste):
- Integration endpoints: POST /v1/chat with conversation_id header; support for streaming + chunked responses.
- Suggested pilot config: batch_size=32, cache_policy=prefix, rerank_trigger=confidence_threshold(0.7).
- Observability hooks: request-level traces, token-breakdown per model, per-route cost attribution.

To-dos for this doc:
- Convert into a 6-slide micro-deck (SE speaker notes) — TODO @Marco
- Add real pilot case numbers (CS contributed) — TODO @Lina
- Create an evaluation harness repo snippet for quick demo — TODO @Theo

End of flashpack.

Notes-to-self: want one real example wallet of numbers (tokens per session, cost delta) to make the pilot pitch concrete. Keep language simple for non-ML buyers; include a one-pager for procurement with Reserved vs Hosted cost anchors.
